question: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was described as the ________by Valentine Chirol.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Father of Indian unrest**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The book 'Indian Unrest' written by Valentine Chirol, Stated Tilak the "Father of Indian unrest".

 
 
• He was also given the title of "Lokmanya" which means accepted by the people.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born on 23rd July 1856 in Maharashtra.
 
• He was an extremist leader and actively participated in the struggles of the Indian national movement.
 
• He stressed the need for self-rule.
 
• He was a prominent Extremist leader.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• He started a Marathi newspaper called "Kesari" and Maratha in English.
 
• He wrote "Arctic Home in the Vedas" and "Gita Rahashya".
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak popularised the Vinayaka Chaturthi festival to be held in public so as to reduce the gap between Brahmins and Non-brahmins.
 
• V. O. Chidambaram is an ardent follower of Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak set up his Indian Home Rule League in April 1916.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak held his first Home Rule meeting at Belgaum. Poona was the headquarters of his league.
